title: ns-next project
description: A Newspeak program of several modules, run by ns-next: `main` is the application's module, instantiated with `packageUsing:` a manifest of the others. Paths are relative to this file, with either separator.

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this schema; ns-next checks only that it is a string.

main.description: The application's module: its root class is instantiated with `packageUsing:` the manifest, then sent `main: platform args:`.

modules.description: The other modules the manifest holds, each reached as `manifest <Name>` by the name its source declares.

scripts.description: Named command lines: `ns-next run --script <name>` and `ns-next bench --script <name>` hand one's arguments to `main:args:`, as if written after `--`; arguments after `--` follow them.

propertyNames.description: A script's name: not empty, and neither beginning nor ending with whitespace.

additionalProperties.description: A script: one string, split into arguments as a POSIX shell splits a command line, on every platform. Unquoted spaces, tabs and newlines separate arguments; '…' holds everything literally; "…" holds everything literally but a backslash before ", \, $, a backtick or a newline; outside quotes a backslash escapes the next character; adjacent parts make one argument, and "" alone is an empty one. Nothing is expanded: $, *, ~ and backticks are literal. An unterminated quote or a backslash at the end is refused.
